angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 300,125 km at 15.22 pc = 0.26 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 65.7220 +/- 0.0129 mas (same row, RUWE 1.12): 15.22 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.4314 +/- 0.0075 solar radii from Tey et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of GJ 238 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..283T/abstract): 300,125 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.4193 +/- 0.0095 solar masses from Tey et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of GJ 238 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..283T/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3485 +/- 140 K from Tey et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of GJ 238 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..283T/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Tey et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of GJ 238 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..283T/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/gj-238.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.791, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
